The work, before the introduction

See how the comparison works.

One priority. Three possibilities. A clear distinction between what the information suggests and what still needs checking.

Illustrative exampleFictional homes A, B, and C. These are not current listings or client results.
The buyer’s priority

“A usable ground-floor room matters to me.”

A

A possible layout fit

The example records suggest a ground-floor room that may fit the buyer’s plans.

What to check
Permitted use, dimensions, and whether the layout works in person.
Next step
Clarify the room’s use before prioritizing a tour.
B

A different tradeoff

The example layout puts the extra room upstairs instead.

What to check
Whether another part of the home could meet the buyer’s stated need.
Next step
Decide whether this compromise is worth exploring.
C

A question still open

The example information does not establish the room’s location or use.

What to check
Ask for a floor plan and clarification. Avoid filling the gap with a guess.
Next step
Get the missing information before comparing fit.

Before you ask

A few useful answers.

Do I have to book a call?

No. You can receive and review the comparison first. A short conversation is optional.

What if no homes fit my search?

I will explain the mismatch and the choices worth reconsidering. The comparison may include fewer than three homes; I will not fill it with unsuitable options.

Can I send homes I have already found?

Yes. Share the listing links and what you like or want to understand. I will check whether the homes are still available and appropriate to include.

Is this an inspection or an appraisal?

No. It organizes available information and questions for further investigation. Inspections, appraisals, lending advice, and legal advice require the appropriate professionals.

What if I already have an agent?

Please tell me before requesting personalized work. Existing representation can affect what assistance is appropriate.

Does this request hire you as my agent?

No. We would discuss services, duration, and negotiable compensation in a separate written buyer representation agreement before touring homes together.
